column1: # Golden set for modules/system/homebeacon, second pass 2026-09-26.
# Judged against the QUOTE, not the sentence. My first pass over run one
# judged three claims from their statements alone and got all three wrong,
# which is the failure the evidence field exists to prevent.
# Run: llmq-claims against qwen2.5-coder 7B on llama-server, min 3, max 4
# claims per subject, 700-token cap, one request per subject over a shared
# prefix, with the instruction rules and quote minLength added after run
# one. 11 claims produced, 11 survived the machine checks, 9 accepted here.
# Against run one's 16 produced, 8 machine-accepted, 6 human-accepted: the
# rules moved the MODEL rather than the filter. Fewer claims, better ones,
# and the machine checks had less to remove because less garbage arrived.
# One rule backfired. Requiring kind=reason to carry confidence=stated made
# the model avoid both labels: every claim here is marked inferred, several
# quoting comments that state the fact outright, and no claim is labelled a
# reason at all. A constraint a model can evade by relabelling is a tax on
# the honest path. Confidence should be DERIVED from where the quote landed
# (comment means stated, code means inferred) rather than chosen.
# verdict
y

column1: # The two rejections, and what each one asks for next:
# keycheck "accepts one argument": the quote is the fail-message helper,
# where $1 is the message being printed. A real quote, read wrongly. No
# mechanical check can catch this; an entailment model asking "does this
# quote support this sentence" is the tool, and it is a different model
# family, so its errors are uncorrelated with the generator's.
# responder "signs a message containing...": the quote is a colon-ended
# lead-in and the three fields are on the lines below it. True statement,
# insufficient evidence. Cheap to catch: require the quote to contain at
# least one identifier that also appears in the statement, which would have
# forced it to quote the message format instead of the sentence announcing
# it.
